_comment: THE NARRATIVE. The 'how you work' page: the only prose in the profile, and the only
part of it a model writes.
scripts/gen_narrative.py emits, all committed, all `git diff --exit-code`'d in CI:
server/builder/narrative_spec.py      Pydantic, extra='forbid', on the way into Postgres
mobile/src/generated/narrative.ts     what the profile screen renders
A field marked `stamped` is written by analysis/narrative.py AFTER the model has
spoken: the version the rules were at, which model wrote it, and what the checks took
back off it. Those are recorded and stored but are NOT in the schema the model sees,
because a model that can write its own dashes_rewritten count can write a zero.
The bounds are stated twice on purpose, exactly as spec/analysis.v1.json explains:
the constrained decoder behind `claude -p --json-schema` honours `required` and
`additionalProperties: false` but not string lengths, so the model reads them in the
description and Pydantic enforces them at the door.

NarrativeClaim.name: text
NarrativeClaim.doc: the claim, in the second person, no numbers needed here.

NarrativeClaim.name: evidence
NarrativeClaim.doc: the numbers behind it, copied from the input. Never a number the input did not contain.

fields.name: archetype_line
fields.doc: what this person's archetype means for THEM, naming the measurement that earned it. Never a definition of the archetype in general. Empty when the check took it back.

fields.name: how_you_work
fields.doc: the shape of their working day: how they open a session, how much rope they give the agent, when they step in, how they verify. Every paragraph cites at least one number from the input.

fields.name: strengths
fields.doc: what they are good at, each with the measurement under it.

fields.name: watch_outs
fields.doc: what the same numbers suggest is costing them, each with the measurement under it. Never a scolding.

fields.name: one_experiment
fields.doc: one concrete thing to try next session, small enough to do, tied to a number above so they can tell whether it worked.

fields.name: narrative_version
fields.doc: == spec version. A retuned prompt is a recompute, not a migration.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: model id that wrote this, as reported by claude -p

fields.name: dashes_rewritten
fields.doc: dashes rewritten as commas after the fact. Rewritten, never rejected: throwing a paid call away over punctuation is not a trade.

fields.name: invented_numbers_dropped
fields.doc: claims deleted because they carried a number the input did not contain. Above zero means the ban is doing work; the claims themselves are logged.
